findings.title: A final console-write exception can contradict the saved driver exit status
findings.function: run_locked, with propagation to the top-level exception handler
static_execution_path: All actual child commands and final checks succeed; passed evaluates to true.
run_locked saves status=finished, result=passed and driver_exit_code=0.
The subsequent unprotected print raises BrokenPipeError or another output OSError.
The exception leaves run_locked without changing the saved record and reaches the top-level failure handler, which exits with code 1.
findings.impact: The durable overall driver result/exit annotation can say passed/0 while the actual driver exits 1. The previously observed inner command exits remain accurate; this finding concerns the overall evidence-finalization outcome.
findings.required_correction: Remove the final success print or make that presentation non-failing after the terminal record is committed. Preserve the exact stock commands, prerequisite, locks, identities and all acceptance limits.
findings.validation_basis: Static control-flow analysis only. No broken-pipe test or driver execution was performed.

limits: Static review does not establish real command success, timing behavior, signal delivery, lock behavior, group quiescence, Elan selection or compiler results.

The 3600-second command deadline initiates cleanup. If killpg(0) still observes a group, including possible zombies, cleanup can retain both locks indefinitely. The code declares this conservative incomplete state rather than claiming a finite cleanup deadline or quiescence from leader exit alone.
The free-space check refuses zero available bytes; it is not a capacity guarantee for the regression workload.

Before/after identities assume the existing stable trusted-checkout discipline; this review does not establish protection against transient hostile rewrites or a general process-enumeration capability.
